rationale: Evidence: iteration 9 (kp 2.5, kd 1.2, ki 0, base 1.2, 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.14 m, wheel track 0.14 m) is the best design so far at 917.5. Oval finishes 20/20 at 2.12 s and s-bend finishes 20/20 at 2.35 s. The slalom finishes 17/20 with 3 off-track exits, 0.15 line-loss events per run, rms 0.012 m and steering oscillation 0.26. Slalom failures cost about 700 points each, so they are the main gap. The kp sweep on the slalom gave 11/20 finishes at kp 2.0 (line-loss 0.6), 16/20 at kp 2.25, and 17/20 at kp 2.5. Line loss falls as kp rises, which points to insufficient turn authority on the tightest bends rather than overshoot. kd has saturated (iteration 8 gave no gain at kd 1.5), and steering oscillation (0.26) and control effort (6.2 on the slalom) still leave headroom. Change: a single-variable change, kp 2.5 to 2.75, with every other value held from iteration 9. Expected result: slalom finish rate of 0.85 to 0.9 with a line-loss rate at or below 0.15, oval and s-bend close to iteration 9 (completion time about 2.1 to 2.4 s). Risk: steering oscillation and control effort rise with kp, and iteration 5 (kp 3.0 with a wider spread) had slalom control effort of 8.0; if oscillation exceeds about 0.35 or the slalom drops below 0.85 finishes, the next step is to return to kp 2.5 and test ki 0.1 for drift, not more kp. Hypotheses: (H1) the remaining slalom off-track exits are a turn-authority limit, so kp 2.75 cuts them; (H2) oval and s-bend are unaffected because the per-cm gain is only slightly higher. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness, to see whether the slalom failures are line loss or overshoot.
